result.title: When Sensors Fail: Coverage Auditing with Incomplete Sensor Records
result.comment: Concise author preprint; 3 pages, 1 table; no supplementary material
result.summary: Sensor outages can conceal prediction-interval coverage deficits behind acceptable marginal performance, while unavailable future readings leave some issued forecasts unscorable. We present a measurement-record audit that links issue-time outage duration, original target availability, and time-uniform statistical evidence. The audit retains complete forecast keys, batches all sensors and overlapping horizons at each measurement tick, and projects simultaneous covered-count and scored-count bounds onto a cumulative conditional expected coverage ratio. This target is distinguished from empirical coverage and outage-conditional population coverage. Selected traffic and air-quality results illustrate the gap between pooled and long-outage coverage; in METR-LA, only 7.6% of issued long-gap forecasts have originally observed targets. Of 30 primary sequential outage-state audits, 26 are inconclusive and four lack scored support. This concise presentation gives the core construction and selected aggregate evidence without the full experimental supplement.

AI.brief_summary: 针对传感器故障场景提出一种基于测量记录的预测区间覆盖率审计：把发布时刻的故障时长、原始目标可得性与时间一致统计证据结合，将同时覆盖计数与可评分计数的界投影为累积条件期望覆盖率，并用交通与空气质量数据说明汇总结论与长时间故障条件下覆盖表现的差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其对「不可评分预测」的剔除与条件覆盖率目标的区分，可能为 latent 轨迹中中间状态无法核验时的证据审计与贡献分配提供概念参照，需较多核查。
